questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: South Korea about 100,295 square kilometres; Georgia about 69,700 square kilometres; Haiti about 27,750 square kilometres; Tonga about 749 square kilometres.

questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Seoul?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of South Korea is Seoul.

questions.prompt: Which continent is South Korea in?

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find South Korea on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find South Korea on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of South Korea?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the South Korea article.

questions.proof: The capital city of South Korea is Seoul.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with South Korea?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture South Korea on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography” part of the South Korea article.

questions.proof: South Korea is in East Asia, bordering North Korea, and is surrounded by water on three sides, as it makes up the southern part of the Korean peninsula.
